prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Active StreamableHTTP SSE streams (both the per-request POST stream and the standalone GET stream) were not being closed when the session manager shuts down, so EventSourceResponse coroutines got cancelled mid-stream, producing ASGI-incomplete-response errors/hung tasks. prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2253 changes two files: it adds a loop in terminate() that closes every entry in _sse_stream_writers, and reorders streamable_http_manager.py's shutdown to terminate sessions gracefully before cancelling the task group -- the latter is the actual ordering fix for the shutdown-time cancellation. #3218 only registers the GET_STREAM_KEY writer into _sse_stream_writers in streamable_http.py; it doesn't touch the manager's shutdown ordering, and without #2253's terminate() loop there is nothing that would close the writer it registers.

prs.title: fix(shared): make UrlElicitationRequiredError pickle-safe
prs.author: ulofiai
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: MCPError (and subclasses like UrlElicitationRequiredError) fail to pickle correctly / lose their payload on pickle round-trip. Default Exception.__reduce_ex__ reconstructs via cls(*self.args), which either drops the ErrorData payload (generic MCPError case, targeted by #2478's 'preserve payload' fix) or raises TypeError for subclasses whose __init__ signature doesn't match args, e.g. UrlElicitationRequiredError(elicitations, message=None) vs stored args (code, message, data) — this is issue #2431, targeted directly by #2555 and #3262. (3 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: MCPError (and subclasses like UrlElicitationRequiredError) fail to pickle correctly / lose their payload on pickle round-trip. Default Exception.__reduce_ex__ reconstructs via cls(*self.args), which either drops the ErrorData payload (generic MCPError case, targeted by #2478's 'preserve payload' fix) or raises TypeError for subclasses whose __init__ signature doesn't match args, e.g. UrlElicitationRequiredError(elicitations, message=None) vs stored args (code, message, data) — this is issue #2431, targeted directly by #2555 and #3262. (3 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: 3262 fixes __reduce__ once on the base MCPError class using MCPError.__new__(error_type) + Exception.__init__(*args) + __dict__ state restore, so every subclass (including UrlElicitationRequiredError) is covered without per-class overrides or special-casing — its updated test file explicitly adds coverage for a second subclass (NoBackChannelError) to prove the generic path works, not just the one class named in the title. #2555 only adds a __reduce__ override on UrlElicitationRequiredError itself, so any other MCPError subclass with a non-matching constructor signature stays broken. #2478 also fixes this generically via a `_restore_mcp_error` helper, but that helper still needs an `if exc_type is UrlElicitationRequiredError` branch to call a different classmethod (`from_error` vs `from_error_data`), so it doesn't fully eliminate per-subclass special-casing the way 3262's __dict__-based restore does, and reconstructing from ErrorData risks not round-tripping instance attributes that aren't derivable from the wire-format data (3262's __dict__ restore preserves them exactly).

clusters.pick_reason: 3262 fixes __reduce__ once on the base MCPError class using MCPError.__new__(error_type) + Exception.__init__(*args) + __dict__ state restore, so every subclass (including UrlElicitationRequiredError) is covered without per-class overrides or special-casing — its updated test file explicitly adds coverage for a second subclass (NoBackChannelError) to prove the generic path works, not just the one class named in the title. #2555 only adds a __reduce__ override on UrlElicitationRequiredError itself, so any other MCPError subclass with a non-matching constructor signature stays broken. #2478 also fixes this generically via a `_restore_mcp_error` helper, but that helper still needs an `if exc_type is UrlElicitationRequiredError` branch to call a different classmethod (`from_error` vs `from_error_data`), so it doesn't fully eliminate per-subclass special-casing the way 3262's __dict__-based restore does, and reconstructing from ErrorData risks not round-tripping instance attributes that aren't derivable from the wire-format data (3262's __dict__ restore preserves them exactly).
